verses.text: As they came near Jerusalem and reached Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples ahead.
He told them, “Go into the village across from you. Right away you’ll find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to me.
If anyone asks you about it, say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and they’ll let you take them right away.”
This happened to fulfill what the prophet had spoken:
“Tell the daughter of Zion, ‘Look, your King is coming to you, humble and riding on a donkey—a colt, the offspring of a donkey.’”
The disciples went and did exactly what Jesus had told them.
They brought the donkey and colt, put their clothes on them, and Jesus sat on them.
A huge crowd spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from trees and spread them along the road.
The crowds walking ahead of him and behind him kept shouting, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name! Hosanna in the highest!”
When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up. People asked, “Who is this?”
The crowds answered, “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee.”
Jesus entered God’s temple and drove out everyone buying and selling there. He overturned the money changers’ tables and the seats of those selling doves.
He told them, “Scripture says, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you’ve turned it into a hideout for robbers!”
Blind and lame people came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
The chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things he did and heard the children shouting in the temple, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” They were angry.
They asked him, “Do you hear what they’re saying?” Jesus replied, “Yes. Haven’t you read, ‘From the mouths of children and nursing babies, you’ve prepared praise’?”
He left them, went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there for the night.
In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree beside the road and went over, but found only leaves. He said to it, “May you never bear fruit again!” The tree withered at once.
When the disciples saw this, they were amazed. “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?” they asked.

Jesus answered, “I’m telling you the truth: if you have faith and don’t doubt, you’ll do not only what happened to this fig tree. You’ll even be able to tell this mountain, ‘Lift up and throw yourself into the sea,’ and it will happen.
Whatever you ask for in prayer with faith, you’ll receive.”
When Jesus entered the temple and was teaching, the chief priests and elders came to him. “By what authority are you doing these things?” they asked. “Who gave you this authority?”
Jesus answered, “I’ll ask you one question too. If you answer me, I’ll tell you by what authority I do these things.
Was John’s baptism from heaven or from people?” They discussed it among themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll ask us, ‘Then why didn’t you believe John?’
But if we say, ‘From people,’ we’re afraid of the crowd, because they all consider John a prophet.”
So they answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” He said to them, “Then I won’t tell you by what authority I do these things.
“What do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first and said, ‘Son, go work in my vineyard today.’
The son answered, ‘I won’t,’ but later changed his mind and went.
The father went to the second son and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’m going, sir,’ but didn’t go.
Which of the two did what their father wanted?” They answered, “The first.” Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God’s Kingdom ahead of you.
John came to show you the way of righteousness, but you didn’t believe him. The tax collectors and prostitutes did believe him. Even after you saw that, you didn’t change your minds and believe him.
“Listen to another parable. A landowner planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress, built a tower, and rented it to farmers. Then he went to another country.
When harvest time came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to collect his fruit.
But the farmers seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
He sent more servants than before, and the farmers treated them the same way.
Finally he sent his son, thinking, ‘They’ll respect my son.’
But when the farmers saw the son, they said to each other, ‘This is the heir. Come on, let’s kill him and take his inheritance.’
They grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
So when the vineyard owner comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
They answered, “He’ll bring those wicked men to a terrible end, then rent the vineyard to other farmers who will give him his share of the crop at harvest time.”
Jesus said to them, “Haven’t you ever read in Scripture, ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the most important cornerstone. The Lord did this, and it’s amazing to us’?
So I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and given to a people who produce its fruit.
Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but it will crush anyone it falls on.”
When the chief priests and Pharisees heard these parables, they realized he was talking about them.
They wanted to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowds, who considered him a prophet.
